home.tagline: Browse your databases through their relations.
home.subtitle: Postgres, MySQL and SQLite, with relations you can follow.

help.title: Help

home.title: How can we help?
home.subtitle: Guides for every part of DbLocal. Search, or start with the basics.

help.noResultsHint: Try a shorter term, or browse the topics on the left.

notFound.title: Article not found
notFound.description: This article does not exist (any more).

ssl.title: SSL / TLS
ssl.text: Encrypts the connection. “Require” encrypts without checking the certificate; the verify modes also check it against your CA.

ssh.title: SSH tunnel
ssh.text: Reaches a database that is only visible from another machine, going through an SSH server you can log in to.

environment.title: Environment and read-only
environment.text: Prod connections ask for extra confirmation before writes. Read-only blocks every write from DbLocal.

virtual.title: Virtual relations
virtual.text: Describe a link the database does not declare as a foreign key. It is stored by DbLocal and never changes your database.

display.title: Display column
display.text: The column shown in foreign key chips and pickers. It is inferred and can be changed per table.

filters.title: Filters
filters.text: Combine conditions with AND / OR groups. Operators depend on the column type, and the filter is part of the URL.

pending.title: Pending changes
pending.text: Edits are held here until you save. Saving runs them in one transaction, so a failure changes nothing.

prod.title: Writing to prod
prod.text: On a prod connection, saving asks you to type the connection name first.

limits.title: Row limit and timeout
limits.text: Results stop at the row limit and a statement is cancelled at the timeout, so a mistake cannot freeze the app.

readonly.title: Read-only sessions
readonly.text: A read-only connection runs queries in a read-only transaction; writes are refused by the database itself.

alertBeforeRun.title: Alert before run
alertBeforeRun.text: When ticked, every run first lists the statements and what each one does, and runs only after you confirm.

historySuggestions.title: History suggestions
historySuggestions.text: While you type, the rest of a query you ran before shows in grey. → or Tab accepts it, ⌥→ takes one word.

layout.title: Diagram layout
layout.text: Tables are placed automatically. Drag them to arrange; positions are saved per schema and can be reset.

overview.title: Notes
overview.text: Free Markdown notes, one per connection and one per table. They stay in DbLocal's own store, never in your database, and save as you type.

overview.title: Functions & triggers
overview.text: Read, create, edit and delete the logic stored in the database. Every change shows the exact SQL and asks before running.

demo.resetBody: The demo goes back to its original data. Everything you changed in it is lost. Your own databases are not affected.

tour.title: Take the 2-minute tour
tour.description: A guided pass over the main flow, on a safe demo database. Your own databases are never touched.

tables.title: Your tables
tables.body: Every table of the schema is listed here. Click one to open it; double-click keeps it as its own tab.

grid.title: The data grid
grid.body: Rows load as you scroll. Sort from a column header, filter from the bar above, and use the arrow keys to move between cells.

children.title: Children, one click away
children.body: Count columns show the records that point at this row. Click “orders” to see only this user's orders.

parents.title: Follow a foreign key
parents.body: A chip is the related record: click it to open it in the side panel, or hover for a preview.

related.title: A filtered view
related.body: This chip says the rows are limited to one user's orders. Remove it to see the whole table again; the address bar always reproduces what you see.

record.title: The record panel
record.body: Every field and every relation of one record. Follow relations from here without leaving the panel.

trail.title: Your trail
trail.body: The breadcrumb remembers where you came from. Use it, or Back and Forward, to retrace your steps.

edit.title: Edit and save
edit.body: Double-click a cell, type a value and press Enter. The change stays pending until you save with the bar at the bottom (Ctrl/⌘ + S), after previewing the SQL. This demo is safe to change.

sql.title: The SQL editor
sql.body: For anything the grid does not cover: autocomplete from your schema, run the statement under the cursor, save queries and see the history.

palette.title: Everything from the keyboard
palette.body: The command palette finds tables, queries and actions, and goes straight to a record with #table id. Press F1 any time for help.

language.title: Choose your language
language.description: You can change it any time in the settings.

notes.connectionPlaceholder: Write anything about this connection: what it is for, who owns it, gotchas, useful queries… Markdown is supported.
notes.tableHint: Markdown notes about this table, saved as you type.
notes.tablePlaceholder: What this table holds, how its columns are used, queries worth keeping… Markdown is supported.

status.error: Could not save the note. Your text is kept; keep typing to retry.

pick.title: Select an item
pick.description: Pick a function, procedure or trigger on the left to read its definition.

routines.mysqlNotAtomic: MySQL cannot undo DDL: editing drops the object and creates it again, so if the new definition fails it stays dropped.
